new_candidates.title: Genomics and social practices at Mogou and other Gansu sites during prehistoric trans-Eurasian exchange
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Genome data from 149 ancient individuals from Mogou and ten other Gansu sites indicate adoption of western-derived crops and livestock without detectable western or central Eurasian genetic influence. At Mogou, close biological relatedness did not strongly determine burial proximity and no first- or second-degree relatives were found among sampled multiple burials. Useful for separating cultural/technical diffusion from demic diffusion and co-burial from biological kinship.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Absence of detectable western/central Eurasian ancestry in the sampled individuals does not prove zero historical contact. Statistical associations between ancestry and burial treatment do not define individual social identity or status deterministically. Co-burial patterns are site-specific and must not be universalized.

primary_or_authoritative_sources: Chinese Academy of Sciences IVPP research release dated 2026-09-03

new_candidates.title: An assemblage of resin-mounted macropod incisors from Quinkan Country, Cape York Peninsula, Queensland
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Twelve macropod incisors with resin residues from Windmill Way were analyzed by microscopy, FTIR, LC-MS and AMS. Two directly dated resin samples place at least part of the assemblage around 1,100-1,300 years ago. Evidence supports personal adornment while leaving single-versus-multiple-object history and semantic or ceremonial meaning unresolved.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Personal-adornment interpretation is supported by resin, fibres, hide and lack of utilitarian wear, but specific ceremonial or symbolic meanings are not established. The authors explicitly reject unsupported trade inference and refrain from assigning ceremonial meaning without evidence. Traditional Owner permissions and cultural context must govern any reuse of rock-art imagery or sensitive knowledge.

provenance.source: Australian Archaeology / Taylor & Francis; publication date cross-checked in public bibliographic reporting

new_candidates.title: Wetland life: Exploring Mesolithic Hunter-Gatherer-Fisher socioecologies using high-resolution palaeoenvironmental reconstructions of pollen and NPP at Dagsmosse, Sweden
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: High-resolution pollen, macrofossil, charcoal and non-pollen-palynomorph reconstruction from Dagsmosse links Mesolithic occupation phases with changing lake ecology, fishing, dwelling and landscape modification. Useful environmental context for testing human-environment interaction without reducing it to passive adaptation.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Palaeoecological proxies support environmental and activity reconstructions but do not establish ritual, cosmological or symbolic motivations. Some causal language about decision-making remains interpretive and should be represented separately from measured proxies.

new_candidates.title: Evaluation of DNA and collagen preservation in Late Pleistocene and Holocene bovid fossils from South Africa
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: The study screens DNA in 144 bovid specimens and collagen in 54 from a 320-specimen documented collection. DNA preservation was detected in 45% of screened specimens and collagen in 35%, with four Late Pleistocene specimens preserving authentic ancient DNA. Site strongly influenced preservation, and specimens were digitally recorded before destructive sampling.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Preservation is site- and age-dependent. Failure to recover biomolecules is not evidence that a taxon, population or behavior was historically absent. Results concern bovid fossils and cannot be transferred mechanically to human remains or other substrates.

new_candidates.title: Genetic continuity and dietary change during the emergence of millet farming in northern China
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Genome-wide and isotope data from eleven Xinglong individuals directly dated to roughly 9,000-5,000 cal BP indicate long regional genetic continuity across the transition toward millet cultivation, with later admixture. Two residential co-burials at different periods contained first-degree relatives. This provides a useful contextual counterpoint to Mogou: co-burial can be kin-structured in one setting and not in another.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Small sample size and site-specific mortuary contexts prevent universal inference about agricultural transitions or co-burial. The study supports context dependence, not a general rule that agriculture spreads without migration or that residential burials are necessarily kin-based.

hypotheses_requiring_human_review.reason: Mogou/Gansu and Xinglong supply complementary empirical cases where subsistence/technology change is not reducible to population replacement.
Directly conflicting site patterns show that co-burial-to-kinship edges must be conditional and evidence-specific.
Quinkan objects warrant object-function review with Traditional Owner cultural-governance flags before any semantic interpretation or image reuse.
Dagsmosse can enrich paleoclimate and niche-construction layers while preserving a boundary between proxy and motivation.
Preservation-aware inference should be explicit in negative-evidence handling.

summary: Five material candidate-only additions: a new Cell ancient-DNA/social-practice study from Gansu; Indigenous Australian directly dated resin-mounted tooth ornaments; two ahead-of-issue Quaternary Science Reviews studies on Swedish Mesolithic paleoecology and South African biomolecular preservation; and a Current Biology ancient-DNA/isotope study of early millet farming. No evidence promotion, historical relationship generation or verified chronology revision occurred.
